questions.prompt: What is the dot product of (2, 1) and (3, −2)?

options.explanation: 8 is 2×3 + 1×2. The second product is 1 × (−2) = −2, so the minus sign must stay.
That is the position-by-position product before the last step. A dot product adds those products into one number.
Right. 2×3 + 1×(−2) = 6 − 2 = 4. Multiply position by position, then add.
3 comes from adding the numbers inside each vector and multiplying the sums: (2+1) × (3−2) = 3 × 1. The dot product multiplies first, then adds.

questions.prompt: Query q = (3, 4). Document C = (6, 8). What is their cosine similarity, and why?

options.text: 1, because C points in exactly the same direction as q.
options.explanation: Right. The dot product is 18 + 32 = 50 and the lengths are 5 and 10, so 50 ⁄ 50 = 1. Cosine ignores length; C is q made twice as long.

options.text: 50, because that is the dot product of q and C.
options.explanation: 50 is the dot product. Cosine similarity divides it by both lengths (5 × 10 = 50), so the result is 1.

options.text: 0.5, because C is twice as long as q, so the score is cut in half.
options.explanation: Cosine similarity does not change with length. Dividing by both lengths removes it, so only the direction counts.

questions.prompt: Your vector store holds OpenAI embeddings, which the OpenAI docs say are normalized to length 1. Why can search use a plain dot product instead of the full cosine formula?

options.text: Because the dot product of any two embeddings is always 1.
options.explanation: Length 1 fixes the size of each vector, not the angle between two of them. Different directions still give different scores.

options.text: Because the bottom of the cosine formula is 1 × 1 = 1, so cosine equals the dot product.
options.explanation: Right. Cosine divides the dot product by both lengths. With both lengths equal to 1, nothing changes, and OpenAI says the dot product is slightly faster.

options.text: Because OpenAI says cosine similarity gives wrong rankings for its embeddings.
options.explanation: OpenAI recommends cosine similarity. The dot product gives the same scores here; it is only cheaper to compute.

options.text: Because normalized vectors can only point in one direction.
options.explanation: A vector of length 1 can point any way. Only its length is fixed, which is why the angle still carries the meaning.
